newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices slip on German state CPI.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices slip on German state CPI.

text.p: Danish bond prices continued to slip on Friday, weighed down by German state CPI figures, after an initial upward surge, a dealer said.
"Inflation has not developed in quite such a negative way as the numbers indicated at first glance," he said, adding that he saw little further movement during the rest of the day.
At 1140 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 110.60, yielding 6.42 percent, in turnover of 3.0 billion crowns. It had closed on Thursday at 110.91.
Its March future fell 0.50 point to 110.04, with 430 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.55 point to 87.40.
The crown traded at 3.8162 per mark, firming slightly from its earlier 3.8167 but still a shade under Thursday's 3.8160.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was 66 basis points, unchanged from the morning but markedly wider than yesterday's 61 bp. --Kenneth Lund Petersen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969659
